item.title: [7] The piezochiral effect
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: A. Cavalleri, P. G. Radaelli

Authors: Z. Zeng, M. Först, M. Fechner, X. Deng, A. Cavalleri, P. G. Radaelli

Score 7/10 C_MAYBE

Why: New strain-responsive functionality for controlling chirality, relevant to electronic symmetry studies.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #piezoelectricity #chirality #topic

Abstract: The piezochiral effect, a new member of the family of strain-responsive functionalities alongside piezoelectricity and piezomagnetism, is introduced, enabling control of chirality through mechanical strain, with future applications in photonics, spintronics, biosensing and quantum information.

item.title: [7] Perpendicular switching of polarization in layered ferroelectrics
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Javier Junquera, Ramamoorthy Ramesh

Authors: Pushpendra Gupta, Sergio Puebla, Fernando Gómez-Ortiz, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Control of polarization in layered oxides; relevant to symmetry-broken phases and electronic structure.

Tags: #Bi4Ti3O12 #ferroelectricity #material

Abstract: Perpendicular switching of the polarization state in the layered ferroelectric Bi4Ti3O12 is demonstrated by means of trilinear coupling, allowing manipulation of the in-plane polarization component with an out-of-plane electric field.

item.title: [7] Electric dipoles go sideways in thin ferroelectric film
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Elzbieta Gradauskaite

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Significant study of unconventional ferroelectricity in thin films, relevant to 2D materials and electronic order.

Tags: #ferroelectricity #thinfilms #quantummaterials

Abstract: Coupling between horizontal and vertical electric polarization enables an unconventional ferroelectric material to be controlled using standard device geometry.
